comparison: Perfect alignment on claims C73-C74 regarding NBD separation in MsbA, but opposite evaluations: OpenEval marks as UNCERTAIN noting the contradiction with DEER data in proteoliposomes, while peer reviewers mark as UNSUPPORTED, explicitly challenging the authors' dismissal of NBD separation as artifactual.

Both address peptidisc structural arrangement claims (C8, C9, C39, C101-C120, C128, C163-C164, C172-C173, C177, C179). OpenEval finds these SUPPORTED with detailed structural evidence, while peer reviewers mark as UNCERTAIN, expressing concerns about ambiguous/weak densities especially for MscS and challenges in unambiguous assignment of peptidisc helices.

Strong agreement on on-gradient reconstitution method and RC complex characterization (C2-C3, C33, C44-C49, C55-C61, C126-C127, C132-C134, C141-C142). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers explicitly acknowledged this as a key contribution without criticism.

Both address universality/versatility claims (C4, C10, C40, C125, C129, C179). OpenEval marks as UNCERTAIN, noting limited test cases don't support broad universality claims. Peer reviewers mark as SUPPORTED, accepting the versatility and adaptability conclusions despite noting some limitations in complete structural characterization.

Both address MsbA structural and functional characterization (C5-C7, C35-C37, C64, C66-C72, C75-C79, C82). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. Agreement on cryo-EM quality, functional data showing increased ATPase activity, and LPS binding preservation.

Strong agreement on lipid preservation claims (C94-C95, C159-C161). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. Agreement that peptidiscs preserve tightly bound lipids (LPS in MsbA) but not loosely associated ones (no lipids visible in MscS).

Both address impact of peptidisc ordering on cryo-EM processing (C175-C178, C180, C185-C188). Both evaluate as UNCERTAIN. OpenEval notes the inference about processing advantages is reasonable but not directly demonstrated; peer reviewers requested clarification on whether theoretical advantages are actually observed.

Overlap on MscS structural claims (C38, C84-C93). OpenEval evaluates MsbA and MscS together as SUPPORTED in R2; peer reviewers separately evaluate MscS structure (R4) as SUPPORTED, accepting the resolution and quality as comparable to nanodiscs.

Overlap on native conformation preservation claims (C122-C123, C154-C157). OpenEval marks as SUPPORTED based on structural and functional evidence; peer reviewers also mark as SUPPORTED, accepting that peptidiscs preserve native conformations, though suggesting stability data could be strengthened.

Both address fluorophore-labeled peptide development (C137-C140). Both evaluate as UNCERTAIN. OpenEval notes preliminary data looks promising but lacks full validation; peer reviewers explicitly requested development and validation of this approach, indicating insufficient support.

Overlap on resolution comparison claims (C150-C153). OpenEval marks as SUPPORTED, noting peptidiscs achieve comparable resolutions to nanodiscs; peer reviewers also mark as SUPPORTED, explicitly stating resolutions were similar though not improved.

Partial overlap on peptidisc utility claims (C4, C40, C179). OpenEval R4 addresses native state preservation broadly; peer R11 addresses versatility/adaptability. Both ultimately support peptidisc effectiveness though OpenEval R9 separately questions universality claims.
